html:
The Quileute are a Native American people of the west coast of the Olympic Peninsula in Washington state. Their main village is La Push, at the mouth of the Quillayute River. Their language is one of only two Chimakuan languages, and its close relative is extinct.

They were skilled seafarers who hunted whales and seals from large cedar canoes, fished for salmon and smelt, and lived in plank houses. Their neighbours included the Makah to the north and the Queets and Quinault to the south.

In 1855 and 1856 they signed the Treaty of Olympia with the Washington Territory. A small reservation at La Push was set up in 1889. The Quileute language has very few speakers today, though the tribe teaches it in its school. The tribe became widely known after the "Twilight" novels used it as a setting.
